about.title: California City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: California City sits in a stretch of Kern County where residents drive long distances, rely on tools and equipment for outdoor work, and use vehicles and parts that must perform as promised. When a product fails — whether it's a defective auto part, faulty tire, malfunctioning appliance, or unsafe consumer good — the harm can be serious and sudden. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This matters in a small city like California City, where getting timely medical care and understanding your options can feel harder without nearby big-city resources. If a defective product has hurt you or someone you love, LawProactive can connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases and can explain what preserving the product and evidence means for your claim.

items.desc: Keeping the defective product, its packaging, and any related receipts can be critical evidence in a strict liability claim. We can connect you with someone who can advise you on protecting that evidence right away.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company was careless. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was after the incident, along with packaging, manuals, and any receipts. This evidence can be important in a claim. Avoid attempting repairs or throwing anything away before speaking with an attorney.
